# Brief: Monday 2 November 2026, about 13:18 UTC
Coverage runs from Friday 30 October, 13:00 UTC. Prices come from web aggregators and news pages, and intraday quotes differ between them.

## Crude oil (Brent, WTI)
- **Friday close, 30 Oct:** Brent's January contract settled at $113.43, up $2.63, and WTI settled at $104.12 (Reuters via CNBC, as relayed by FinanceFeeds, 1 Nov). The expired December Brent contract settled at $117.64. Brent gained 13.6% in October.
- **OPEC+, Sunday 1 Nov:** OPEC+ agreed to keep December production targets steady (FXStreet, 2 Nov). According to Reuters' sources, this changes little because most Gulf members are below quota anyway (FinanceFeeds). FinanceFeeds lists the next meeting as 29 November, which sets 2027. Saudi Arabia increased its crude exports in October.
- **Monday move, 2 Nov:** Brent traded around $108.5 on Monday morning, down roughly 2.8% from Friday's close, as Iranian negotiators held talks in Qatar on a plan to reopen Hormuz. Other morning quotes were higher. Reuters had Brent at $111.84 and WTI at $102.56 early on Monday. WTI traded around $101.20 in Asian hours.
- **Hormuz and Iran:**
  - **Reopening plan:** Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi said over the weekend that the plan could reopen the strait in as little as two days, provided Washington met a series of conditions.
  - **US position:** Secretary of State Rubio said Trump would like to resolve the war "diplomatically" (CNBC, 2 Nov). Trump kept military options open, and Netanyahu reportedly pressed him to strike Iran once Tuesday's midterm voting is over.
  - **Tanker incidents:** On Sunday UKMTO said a tanker in the strait was hit by an unknown projectile. Iran claimed another ship on the southern route hit a mine and caught fire, per Fars (CBS live blog). That claim could not immediately be verified.
  - **Friday drone claim:** Iran said it destroyed a US sea drone, and the US denied it (Middle East Monitor).
  - **Flows:** IMO data showed at least 30 vessels, mostly oil tankers, hit in October (CNBC, 30 Oct). Tankers still ship substantial crude through the strait, in stark contrast to March.
- **US inventories:** I found no new EIA data in this window. The only figure I saw was from an aggregator, which listed US crude stocks at 410.6 million barrels for the week to 23 October, a 1.9 million barrel draw (worldoilmonitor). That predates the window and I could not check it against EIA.
- **Demand:** China's official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 in October (FXStreet headline, 2 Nov). I found nothing else on demand.

## Gold
- **Friday, 30 Oct:** Spot gold fell 3.6% to $3,875 an ounce (ABC News Australia, 2 Nov).
- **Monday, 2 Nov:** Gold rebounded to near $3,900, and FXStreet's headline puts it near $3,900 despite inflation worries. APMEX showed spot at $3,922, up 0.79% (7:40 ET). BullionVault showed $3,906 at 07:30 GMT.
- **Context (FXStreet, 2 Nov):**
  - Gold trades around 30% below its all-time high near $5,600 set in January.
  - Since the war began in late February, the metal has largely moved opposite oil.
  - Gold did not gain from the tech sell-off, as traders sold it to meet margin calls.

## US equities (S&P 500)
- **Friday close, 30 Oct:** The S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,580.07. The Nasdaq lost 2.86% to 25,437.00, its worst day since June. The Dow fell 1.09% to 51,770.31. (CNBC)
- **Month of October:** The Nasdaq fell 5.3%, its steepest monthly drop since March 2025. The S&P 500 declined 0.9% and the Dow added 1.7%.
- **Cause given for Friday:** Traders moved out of key AI-related stocks into more defensive areas. Selling intensified in the afternoon on month-end profit-taking and ahead of the midterm elections.
- **Earnings:** JP Morgan calculates that more than 80% of S&P 500 companies reporting so far beat EPS estimates (ABC, 2 Nov). AMD, Arista and Supermicro report Tuesday (24/7 Wall St., 2 Nov). Apple and Qualcomm report later this week (CNBC).
- **Monday session:** I found no confirmed S&P 500 level for Monday. A 24/7 Wall St. page showed S&P 500 at 7,612.40, up 0.33%. It does not say whether that is a futures or cash quote, so treat it as unconfirmed.

## US Treasuries and the Federal Reserve
- **Fed decision, Wednesday 28 Oct (just before the window):** The Fed held its target range at 3.75%–4.00%. The hold followed a September increase (Serrari Group). Chairman Kevin Warsh said the bank remained focused on "price stability" (CNBC, 28 Oct).
- **December odds:** CME FedWatch put the odds of a 25 bp hike at the Dec. 9 meeting at 85.7% on 28 Oct. Trading Economics now cites roughly a 75% probability of a December hike. I could not date that figure.
- **Yields, early Monday 2 Nov:** The 10-year was at 4.914%, down 1 bp. The 30-year was at 5.284%. The 2-year was at 4.589%, up 1 bp. (CNBC)
- **Friday, 30 Oct:** Treasurys were boosted by the equity sell-off as investors sought safe havens. The 10-year is near a seven-week low, well below October's peak of 5.36%, its highest since 2002 (FXStreet).
- **Coming up:** On Wednesday the Treasury sets out its planned auction sizes for notes and bonds. Tuesday's midterm results are also in focus. I found no new Fed speeches or data releases dated within the window.

**Caveats:** Several oil and gold figures come from aggregator sites, and quotes differ between sources. The tanker-mine reports are Iranian claims and no maritime authority has confirmed them. I did not use one aggregator page showing a Brent "close" for 2 November, because the day was not over when I searched.

# Brief for Tuesday 3 November 2026 (news since Sunday 1 November, 13:18 UTC)

Price quotes come from aggregator sites. They differ by timestamp and contract, so treat the levels as approximate.

## Crude oil (Brent and WTI)

- **OPEC+ (1 Nov):** OPEC+ kept December production targets unchanged at a meeting on 1 November. The decision on 2027 quotas moved to a meeting of the full group on 29 November. Reuters expects the capacity review that will set 2027 baselines by mid-November. (Source: The Beaver Business, citing Reuters.)
- **Prices fell on Monday 2 Nov:** The S&P 500 ended lower as oil prices tumbled on optimism about a potential US-Iran peace agreement. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Trump would like to resolve the Iranian war "diplomatically." (Reuters via Investing.com and CNBC, 2 Nov.)
- **Closing levels:** Brent closed at $104.19 on 2 Nov. WTI closed near $96.23 (worldoilmonitor.com). The prior Friday (30 Oct) closes were WTI $103.74 and Brent $116.09. (oilpriceapi.com)
- **Tuesday 3 Nov:** oilprice.com showed WTI at $98.13 (+1.73%) and Brent at $106.0 (+1.21%). Investing.com showed WTI near $97.17. CNBC said renewed Middle East tensions pushed oil prices higher on Tuesday.
- **Hormuz and Iran (2–3 Nov):**
  - US forces launched limited defensive strikes on Iranian targets near the Strait of Hormuz, US officials told CBS News on Monday evening.
  - A US official said the strike on Qeshm Island responded to Iran firing at a US aircraft.
  - Iran's Navy claimed another oil tanker caught fire after hitting a sea mine near the eastern entrance to the strait, according to Fars News Agency. This is an Iranian claim. (CBS News)
  - Iran offered to open the Strait of Hormuz on several conditions, and Trump has warned he is open to authorizing major combat operations after the midterms. Iran is demanding sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets. (The Hill, 2 Nov)
  - A tracker site said the strait remains closed to commercial traffic. (straits.live, 3 Nov)
- **US inventories and demand:** I found nothing new. The latest inventory figure that turned up was US crude stocks of 410.6 million barrels for the week to Oct 23, a 1.9 million barrel draw. That is before the window. I found no demand news in the window.

## Gold

- **Monday 2 Nov:** Spot gold rose about 1.9% to roughly $3,965–3,967 per ounce. (APMEX, last updated 11/2 4:20 PM ET; bullion.com, 4:59 PM ET.) JM Bullion said this followed Friday's sharp selloff, when gold fell below $4,000 on inflation concerns, the prospect of higher rates and weak tech stocks.
- **Tuesday 3 Nov:** Quotes differ.
  - Kitco had $3,900.30 at 7:10 a.m. ET, down $45.40.
  - BullionVault showed about $3,935 at 12:57 GMT.
  - JM Bullion showed $3,950.59 at 8:16 AM EST.
- I found no gold-specific news beyond price moves.

## US equities (S&P 500)

- **Monday 2 Nov close:** The S&P 500 shed 0.51% to close at 7,541.40, and the Nasdaq dipped 1.07% to 25,164.32. Both had been up as much as 1.4% and 1.1%. The Dow closed higher (CNBC, 2 Nov).
- **Sectors and breadth:** Seven of the 11 S&P sectors rose, led by consumer discretionary (+2.25%) and materials (+1.83%). (Reuters via Investing.com)
- **Context:**
  - The Nasdaq and S&P 500 each lost ground in October amid AI spending concerns, and the Nasdaq had its worst losses since March 2025. (CNBC)
  - The S&P 500 trades at about 19 times expected earnings, its lowest valuation since 2023. (Reuters)
  - LSEG data shows Q3 S&P 500 earnings on track to rise over 30% year over year.
  - Apple reports quarterly results and US midterm elections are held on Tuesday.
- I found no Tuesday session close yet.

## US Treasuries and the Federal Reserve

- **Monday 2 Nov:** The 10-year yield was down more than 2 bp at 4.906%, the 30-year eased 3 bp to 5.279%, and the 2-year rose more than 1 bp to 4.594%. Treasury set out its planned auction sizes for notes and bonds. (CNBC)
- **Tuesday 3 Nov (CNBC, 4:51 AM EST):** The 10-year was up more than 2 bp at 4.9167%, the 30-year was up 1 bp at 5.2879%, and the 2-year was up more than 1 bp at 4.5956%. CNBC cited voting in the midterms, a busy week of economic data and renewed Middle East tensions.
- **Federal Reserve:** I found no new Fed decision or official statement in the window. The latest policy facts are from before it: the Fed held its key rate in a range of 3.75% to 4% at its October meeting. (CNBC, 29 Oct) The Treasury par-yield page also showed the fed funds target at 3.75–4.00%.

# Brief for Wednesday 4 November 2026 (window: since Monday 2 November, 13:18 UTC)

## Crude oil (Brent, WTI)
- **Monday 2 Nov settlement:** Brent settled 7.63% lower at $104.77 and WTI dropped 7.36% to $96.46 (Gulf News). The fall followed a draft proposal to end the US-Iran war that circulated after Iranian negotiators left Qatar (OilPrice.com).
- **Tuesday 3 Nov:** Prices rebounded in the morning after US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island. WTI was at $98.06 and Brent at $106.61 (EnergyNow). The gains faded by the close. Front-month prices as of 3 Nov were WTI $96.83 and Brent $104.43 (Valor).
- **Wednesday 4 Nov, early trade:** Brent was up 0.8% at $104.42 and WTI up 0.5% at $96.59 by 05:10 GMT (Sabq). I found no later price print.
- **Hormuz and Iran, Monday 2 Nov:** The US struck Iran's Qeshm Island after the IRGC said it had downed a US MQ-9 drone (Jerusalem Post). US officials called the strikes defensive and said they did not appear to signal a resumption of major combat operations (Jerusalem Post).
- **Hormuz and Iran, Tuesday 3 Nov:** Iran said it could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within two days if the US accepts certain demands (Townhall, 3 Nov). Qatari and other mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to stop attacks in the Strait in return for US concessions (CBS News).
- **Hormuz and Iran, Wednesday 4 Nov:** Iran's military said four oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines while trying to pass through the Strait (CBS News live updates). This is Iran's own claim. The same page notes that ships continue to come under attack despite signs of a diplomatic push.
- **OPEC+:** I found nothing new. The seven core members' last confirmed decision was on 4 October, when they kept November targets steady (Reuters via Euronext). Their next meeting was set for 1 November. That date is before this window, and my searches returned no report of its outcome.
- **US inventories and demand:** I found nothing new. No EIA or API stock data came up. One Investing.com summary mentions below-average domestic inventories, but it gives no figures or date.
- **Data note:** One price-API table lists different 2 Nov figures (WTI $98.70, Brent $107.33) from the settlements above. I used the settlement figures.

## Gold
- **Latest quote found:** Kitco showed $3,929.40 per ounce at 5:22 p.m. ET on 3 Nov, down $16.30 on the day. The day's range was $3,894.80 to $3,971.70.
- **Earlier on 3 Nov:** Goldprice.com showed $3,901.99 at 4:21 AM ET, down 1.35%.
- **Other quotes:** Sources differ. BullionVault shows about $4,005 without a clear timestamp. I did not rely on a JM Bullion page showing $4,039 because its dating looked unreliable.
- **Drivers:** I found no news article explaining gold's moves in this window.

## US equities (S&P 500)
- **Monday 2 Nov close:** 7,541.40, down 38.67 points (-0.51%) (Yahoo Finance).
- **Tuesday 3 Nov close:** S&P 500 +27.52 points (+0.36%) to 7,568.92, Nasdaq Composite +0.83% to 25,372.01, Dow -197 points to 51,792.19 (InvestingLive). Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom each gained more than 2%. Decliners outnumbered advancers 318 to 167 in the S&P 500.
- **Context:** The record high is 7,844.52, set on 6 Oct 2026 (TradingView).
- **Midterms:** A Motley Fool article dated 4 Nov says Democrats have retaken the House and Senate. This is a single non-wire source, and I did not verify it elsewhere.
- **Wednesday 4 Nov:** I found no pre-market or intraday S&P 500 data.

## US Treasuries and the Federal Reserve
- **Monday 2 Nov:** The 10-year yield fell 2 basis points and the 2-year rose by more than 1 basis point (CNBC). The Treasury par curve for 2 Nov showed the 10-year at 4.91% and the 2-year at 4.59%.
- **Tuesday 3 Nov:** Yields rose as voting began in the midterms (CNBC). At one point the 10-year was at 4.96%, the 30-year at 5.332% and the 2-year at 4.623%. A later CNBC update had the 10-year at 4.935%, the 30-year at 5.309% and the 2-year at 4.608%. I found no closing levels.
- **Data:** September JOLTS job openings came in better than expected (CNBC, 3 Nov).
- **Fed:** I found no new Fed decisions or speeches in this window. The most recent policy action was the October meeting, when the Fed held its key rate in a range of 3.75% to 4% (CNBC, 29 Oct). That is before this window.
- **Scheduled this week:** ISM services PMI and ADP employment on Wednesday, and October nonfarm payrolls and unemployment on Friday (CNBC).

**Limits:** I used six searches. Several figures are intraday or from aggregator pages, not official closes. I found nothing new on OPEC+, US inventories, gold drivers or the Fed.
